content: Read make.fun/skill.md?ga=1568735676.1794654602.1795037107 and enter the bounty "Forecast GTA VI's launch-day Twitch viewers hour by hour" (make.fun/bounty/gta6-twitch-ccu-forecast-01) as my make.fun account @budybozz: connect to it first (makefun login, then send me the approval link).
I'll read the make.fun skill and check the competition status for gta6-twitch-ccu-forecast-01.
Checking competition status and downloading kit.
Examining kit structure, rules, starter code, and practice inputs.
Analyzing practice inputs to understand comparable structure and identify rolling-midnight launch pattern.
Writing initial forecast model (v1) - normalize all comparables by hour-1, compute median/quantiles.
Testing v1 on p00 - produced flat forecasts, normalization failed to capture curve shapes.
Debugging: analyzing all 19 comparables to classify launch patterns. Found 3 rolling-midnight (RDR2, GoW, Spider-Man 2) and 16 global-simultaneous.
Verifying practice cases p01/p02/p03 are the rolling-midnight games with checkpoint=checkpoint_1.
Writing improved model (v2) - filter to rolling-midnight comparables only, normalize by launch day hour 0, compute quantile bands with winsorizing.
Testing v2 on p00 - still flat, debugging quantile computation. Found winsorize bug (p99 index out of bounds).
Testing again - still flat. Found off-by-one in normalization anchor: competition hour 1 = launch day hour 0 (index 0), not index 1.
Rewrote main.ts with correct normalization (hour 0 = competition hour 1), proper I/O format, and rolling-midnight filtering.
Testing v3 on all practice cases - produces proper rolling-midnight curve with quantile spread.
Verified deterministic output and correct format. Initializing git repo, committing, creating GitHub repo.
Git repo initialized, makefun anchor created (d2d92ca21f14539874f900f5491edd401cb77be1 round 34078315), committed, pushed to GitHub.
Creating transcript bundle and submitting entry.
